name: Groom a dog and trim nails
blurb: Nail trimming is the routine care task most owners dread and most dogs hate — almost always because it was never introduced gradually. Cooperative care fixes it.
gear: A brush suited to the coat type
steps: Learn cooperative care: build a consent signal, take one paw at a time, and stop the moment the dog withdraws.
Spend a week just touching paws and rewarding, before any clippers appear.
Introduce the clippers as a thing that predicts treats, without cutting anything, for several sessions.
Learn where the quick is — the blood vessel inside the nail — and take small slices rather than one big cut. On dark nails, go a sliver at a time and watch the cut surface.
Do one nail a day rather than all of them at once, at first.
Brush regularly to the skin, not just over the top, and learn your dog’s coat type and what it needs.
tips: Cutting the quick hurts and bleeds, and one bad experience can create years of nail-trim fear. Go slowly.
Nails that click on the floor are too long. Regular small trims beat occasional big ones.
proof: Your dog stands calmly for a full nail trim and grooming session without restraint.
